title: Prabhas Held Up Three Fingers and the Internet Lost Its Mind: Inside Netflix's 'Baahubali: The Torchbearer'
excerpt: A four-part documentary revisits the making of Indian cinema's most ambitious franchise — and its final moments just lit the fuse on Baahubali 3 speculation.
body:
The clip is barely thirty seconds long, and it has already set fire to every corner of the Indian internet.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=tHGWBT0Ewuw

https://x.com/NetflixIndia/status/2070821071365030122

In the closing moments of Baahubali: The Torchbearer — a four-part Netflix documentary that dropped globally on June 26 — Rana Daggubati leans forward, half-grinning, half-confessing. "I don't know if I should say this publicly," he begins, "but since Rajamouli and Shobu *garu* aren't here, I'll just say what's on my mind." A beat. "The world may not be ready yet, but there will be more Baahubali!"

The screen cuts to Prabhas, who says nothing. He doesn't need to. He simply raises three fingers — slow, deliberate, unmistakable — and smiles. Beside him, Anushka Shetty breaks into laughter, the kind that says *I know something you don't*. Then the screen goes black. Five words appear: "And the legacy continues..."

No official confirmation. No release date. No press note. Just a gesture, a grin, and the most loaded ellipsis in Indian cinema history.

The Documentary That Brought Mahishmati Back to Life

Before that electrifying tease, *The Torchbearer* spends roughly two and a half hours doing something equally extraordinary: making you fall in love with the Baahubali franchise all over again.

The four-episode series — available in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and Malayalam — reunites SS Rajamouli, Prabhas, Rana Daggubati, Anushka Shetty, Ramya Krishnan, Tamannaah Bhatia, Sathyaraj, Nassar, and producer Shobu Yarlagadda to recount the absurdly ambitious journey of making two films that cost over ₹400 crore, broke every box office record in the country, and turned a Telugu production house into a global brand.

What emerges is less a standard behind-the-scenes featurette and more a war story. Financial crises that nearly shut down production. VFX teams learning on the job because nobody in India had attempted anything at this scale before. Physical toll — Prabhas, we learn, essentially gave five uninterrupted years of his life to one character. And Rajamouli himself, the architect of it all, confessing that there were days he genuinely didn't know if the second film would ever be completed.

> "From production setbacks to financial crises, the Baahubali cast and crew recount the demanding journey behind the beloved epic film series." — Netflix

Producer Shobu Yarlagadda, speaking ahead of the release, described the series as a tribute to the franchise's 10-year journey — its creative process, its influence on popular culture, and the artists and technicians who made it possible.

A Franchise That Rewrote the Rules

For the diaspora, especially, *Baahubali* wasn't just a film — it was a cultural event. Baahubali: The Beginning (2015) shattered records with over ₹600 crore worldwide, but it was the sequel, Baahubali 2: The Conclusion (2017), that entered a different orbit entirely — crossing ₹1,800 crore globally and turning Prabhas into the first true Pan-India superstar of the streaming age.

In the US, UK, and Canada, it was the film that NRI families dragged their American-born kids to see, the one that made non-Telugu-speaking uncles learn who Kattappa was, the one that made "Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?" a genuine water-cooler question from New Jersey to Hounslow.

The franchise has since spawned three novels (*The Rise of Sivagami*, *Chaturanga*, *Queen of Mahishmathi*), animated series (*The Lost Legends*, *Crown of Blood*), graphic novels, and a combined theatrical version — Baahubali: The Epic (2025) — that clocked a staggering 225 minutes and included a mid-credits animated sequence setting up Baahubali: The Eternal War, a two-part animated feature slated for 2027 and 2028, directed by award-winning filmmaker Ishan Shukla.

So the universe is expanding. The question is: will Rajamouli himself return to it?

The Rajamouli Problem

Here's the honest truth: don't expect Baahubali 3 anytime soon. Rajamouli is deep into pre-production on Varanasi, his next epic with Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra, and Prithviraj Sukumaran — which just received a roaring response at the Annecy Film Festival. That film is slated for April 2027, and Rajamouli doesn't do half-measures. A Baahubali 3, if it happens, is likely years away.

But the fact that the stars are openly teasing it — on a Netflix documentary, no less — suggests this isn't idle talk. Something is brewing. Whether it's a direct sequel or an expansion of the animated universe, the legacy, as the title card promises, continues.

Where to Watch

Baahubali: The Torchbearer is streaming now on Netflix worldwide, in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, and Malayalam. Four episodes, each under 40 minutes. Perfect weekend binge for anyone who ever felt a chill when Amarendra Baahubali lifted that golden Shivaling.
